title: Cell theory; prokaryotic, eukaryotic, plant and animal cells
blurb: State the cell theory and tell prokaryotic, eukaryotic, plant and animal cells apart from the structures they contain.
question: A lab slide shows a tiny single cell with ribosomes, a circular chromosome and a peptidoglycan wall, but no nucleus. A second slide shows a cell with a nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts and a cellulose wall. What kind of cell is each, and which features prove it?

teach.body: Formal version: (1) all living things are made of one or more cells; (2) the cell is the basic unit of structure and function of life; (3) all cells come from pre-existing cells. The theory grew from the work of Schleiden, Schwann and Virchow. Plain English: if it is alive, it is built from cells, the cell is the smallest thing that is alive, and new cells only appear when an existing cell divides.

teach.caption: "Pro" means before and "karyon" means kernel (nucleus): prokaryotes evolved before the nucleus did. "Eu" means true: eukaryotes have a true nucleus.
Cell walls: bacteria usually have one (peptidoglycan); among eukaryotes, plants (cellulose) and fungi (chitin) do, animals do not.

teach.h: What every cell has in common
teach.body: Whatever the cell type, four things are always present: a cell (plasma) membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA. Prokaryotes are not "missing" DNA or ribosomes; they make proteins and copy their DNA like any cell. What they lack is a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. That single difference is the fastest way to sort a cell on the exam.

teach.caption: Both are eukaryotic, so both have a nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi and ribosomes.
Note the rigid cell wall outside the membrane and the large central vacuole: animal cells have neither. Plant cells have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.

teach.body: Maya, a pre-nursing student, compares two slides. Slide 1: a cell about 2 micrometers long with ribosomes, a circular chromosome, plasmids and a peptidoglycan wall, but no nucleus. No nucleus means prokaryote, and peptidoglycan means a bacterium. Slide 2: a cell with a nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, a large central vacuole and a cellulose wall. The nucleus makes it eukaryotic; chloroplasts, the central vacuole and cellulose make it a plant cell.

teach.text: Two classic traps: "prokaryotes have no ribosomes or DNA" (they have both; they lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles) and "plant cells have chloroplasts instead of mitochondria" (plants have both and carry out cellular respiration too).

items: Cell theory: all life is cells; the cell is the basic unit; cells come from pre-existing cells.
Prokaryotes (bacteria, archaea): no nucleus, no membrane organelles, circular DNA, binary fission.
Eukaryotes (animals, plants, fungi, protists): nucleus, membrane organelles, linear chromosomes.
Every cell has a membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA.
Plant cells add a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole; animal cells have centrioles.

summary: You can now state the three parts of the cell theory and classify a cell as prokaryotic or eukaryotic, plant or animal, from the structures it contains. You also know which features all cells share, so you will not fall for the "no ribosomes" or "no mitochondria" traps.

A.q: Which statement is one of the three tenets of the cell theory?
options: All cells arise from pre-existing cells
All cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus
All cells are enclosed by a rigid cell wall
All cells make ATP inside mitochondria
A.why: The cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.

whyNot.1: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria and archaea) have no nucleus, so this cannot be a universal tenet.
whyNot.2: Animal cells have no cell wall, so a wall is not part of the cell theory.
whyNot.3: Prokaryotes have no mitochondria, yet they are living cells.

A.q: A single-celled organism has ribosomes, a circular chromosome in a nucleoid region, and a peptidoglycan cell wall. How should it be classified?
options: Fungus, since it has a rigid cell wall
Prokaryote, since it lacks a nucleus
Plant cell, since it has a cell wall
A.why: DNA in a nucleoid (no nucleus) marks a prokaryote, and a peptidoglycan wall marks a bacterium.

whyNot.0: All cells have ribosomes, so ribosomes cannot show that a cell is eukaryotic.
whyNot.1: Fungi are eukaryotes with a nucleus and chitin walls, not peptidoglycan.
whyNot.3: Plant cells have a nucleus and cellulose walls, not a nucleoid and peptidoglycan.

A.q: Which pair of structures is present in a typical plant cell but absent from a typical animal cell?
A.why: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall and chloroplasts; animal cells have neither.

whyNot.0: Animal cells have mitochondria too, so mitochondria do not distinguish the two.
whyNot.1: Centrioles are usually found in animal cells, not plant cells.
whyNot.3: Both cell types have a nucleus; only the vacuole half of this pair is plant-specific.

B.q: Which set of structures is found in BOTH prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
B.why: Every cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA.

whyNot.2: Prokaryotes lack mitochondria, and animal cells lack a cell wall.
whyNot.3: The Golgi apparatus is a membrane-bound organelle, so prokaryotes do not have one.

B.q: A classmate says bacteria cannot make proteins because they have no membrane-bound organelles. Which correction is accurate?
options: Bacteria have 70S ribosomes that make protein
Bacteria take ready-made protein from the host
Bacteria build protein on the rough ER surface
Bacteria make protein inside a small nucleus
B.why: Ribosomes are not membrane-bound, so prokaryotes have them (the smaller 70S type) and use them for protein synthesis.

whyNot.1: Bacteria synthesize their own proteins; many live freely with no host at all.
whyNot.2: Rough ER is a membrane-bound organelle, which prokaryotes do not have.
whyNot.3: Bacteria have no nucleus; their DNA sits in a nucleoid region.

B.q: A culture of Staphylococcus doubles in number every 30 minutes. By which process are the new cells produced?
B.why: Prokaryotes such as Staphylococcus divide by binary fission.

whyNot.0: Mitosis is the division of a eukaryotic nucleus; bacteria have no nucleus.
whyNot.2: Meiosis makes gametes in eukaryotes and halves the chromosome number.
whyNot.3: Budding is how yeast (a eukaryotic fungus) reproduces, not bacteria.

C.q: Which description fits the DNA of a human liver cell but NOT the DNA of a bacterium?
options: One circular chromosome plus small plasmids
Circular DNA free in a nucleoid region
Linear DNA lying loose in the cytoplasm
C.why: Eukaryotic DNA is organized as multiple linear chromosomes wound around histone proteins inside the nucleus.

whyNot.0: A single circular chromosome with plasmids is the prokaryotic arrangement.
whyNot.2: A nucleoid region holds prokaryotic DNA; a liver cell keeps its DNA in a nucleus.
whyNot.3: Eukaryotic linear DNA is enclosed in the nucleus, not loose in the cytoplasm.

C.q: Jordan, a nursing applicant, views a cell with a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell wall made of chitin, but no chloroplasts. What kind of cell is it?
C.why: A nucleus makes it eukaryotic, and a chitin wall is the signature of fungi.

whyNot.0: Plant walls are made of cellulose, and a leaf cell would contain chloroplasts.
whyNot.1: Bacteria have no nucleus or mitochondria, and their walls are peptidoglycan.
whyNot.2: Animal cells have no cell wall at all.

C.q: Which statement about plant and animal cells is INCORRECT?
options: Plant cells and animal cells both have mitochondria
A central vacuole keeps plant cells turgid
Animal cells lack a rigid outer cell wall
Plant cells use chloroplasts, not mitochondria
C.why: This is the false statement: plant cells have chloroplasts for photosynthesis AND mitochondria for cellular respiration.

whyNot.0: True: both plant and animal cells have mitochondria.
whyNot.1: True: the large central vacuole maintains turgor pressure in plant cells.
whyNot.2: True: animal cells have no cell wall.

reteach.title: A studio apartment vs a house
reteach.question: Think of a studio apartment, where everything happens in one open room, and a house, where cooking, sleeping and paperwork each have their own room. Which is the prokaryote?

blocks.body: A prokaryote is the studio: the DNA (the paperwork) sits in an open corner called the nucleoid, with no walls around it, and every job happens in one shared space. A eukaryote is the house: the DNA is locked in an office (the nucleus) and other jobs have their own walled rooms (mitochondria, ER, Golgi). Both homes still have outer walls (a membrane), furniture (cytoplasm), tools (ribosomes) and paperwork (DNA).

A plant cell is a house with a brick wall around the yard (the cellulose cell wall), solar panels on the roof (chloroplasts) and a big water tank (the central vacuole). It still has a furnace (mitochondria). An animal cell is a house with no brick wall, no solar panels and only small storage closets.

blocks.text: Solar panels do not replace the furnace: plant cells have chloroplasts AND mitochondria.

explain.body: Three tenets: all living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells come from pre-existing cells. Cells never assemble from nonliving matter.

test.q: Which observation BEST supports the tenet that all cells come from pre-existing cells?
options: Dividing cells replace worn skin cells
Bacteria are smaller than human cells
Plant cell walls are made of cellulose
test.why: New skin cells are produced when existing cells divide, which is exactly what the third tenet describes.

whyNot.0: Mitochondria numbers relate to energy demand, not to where cells come from.
whyNot.2: Cell size differences say nothing about the origin of new cells.
whyNot.3: Wall composition describes plant structure, not cell origin.

explain.body: Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotes have neither: their DNA lies in a nucleoid region. Everything else (size, DNA shape, ribosome size) follows from this split.

test.q: What is the defining structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Whether the cell has a nucleus
Whether the cell has a membrane
test.why: Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus; prokaryotes do not.

whyNot.1: Both cell types store their genetic information in DNA.
whyNot.3: Every cell is bounded by a cell membrane.

explain.body: No nucleus, so the single circular chromosome sits in the nucleoid. Extra small DNA rings called plasmids may be present. Smaller 70S ribosomes make proteins in the cytoplasm. Most bacteria have a peptidoglycan wall, and they divide by binary fission.

test.q: In a prokaryotic cell, the main chromosome is located in a region called the:
test.why: The nucleoid is the region of a prokaryotic cell where the circular chromosome sits, with no membrane around it.

whyNot.0: A nucleus is a membrane-bound compartment that prokaryotes lack.
whyNot.1: The nucleolus is inside a eukaryotic nucleus and makes ribosomal RNA.
whyNot.2: A nucleosome is DNA wrapped around histones, a eukaryotic arrangement.

explain.body: Plant cells add a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Animal cells have no wall, usually have centrioles and have prominent lysosomes. Both have mitochondria.

test.q: Which plant cell structure is made mainly of cellulose and gives the cell rigid support?
test.why: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose and provides rigid support and protection.

whyNot.0: The cell membrane is a flexible phospholipid bilayer, not cellulose.
whyNot.2: The central vacuole stores water and maintains turgor, but it is not made of cellulose.
whyNot.3: The cytoskeleton is built from protein filaments such as actin and tubulin.
